protocol.name: zext_toplevel_export_v1
protocol.description:
EXPERIMENTAL DRAFT — spatial-os `zext` namespace. Interfaces will be renamed (xx_*, then ext_*) if and when proposed to wayland-protocols; see protocols/README.md for the governance posture and docs/architecture/foreign-session-integration.md for the design rationale. Requirement numbers (R1..R22) refer to docs/research/32-toplevel-export-prior-art.md §8.
This protocol lets a "producer" compositor delegate individual toplevel windows — the client's own buffer stream, the full surface tree, and an input back-path — to a "consumer" compositor (e.g. an XR compositor that composes the windows as floating quads). It is presentation-grade delegation, not screen capture: buffers are the client's original dmabuf allocations (R5), presentation is paced by the consumer (R11-R14), and the producer retains all shell authority over its clients (serials, grabs, popup placement, activation tokens — R15, R17, R18).
Privilege model (R2, R21): the manager global must only be exposed to authorized consumer connections (compositor policy, e.g. security-context based filtering). Toplevel enumeration (ext-foreign-toplevel-list) grants neither export nor input authority. The producer may deny or redact any surface (lock screens, protected content, internal surfaces).

interface.name: zext_toplevel_export_manager_v1
interface.description: The privileged entry point advertised by the producer.

request.name: export_toplevel
request.description: Requests export of the toplevel identified by the given ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 (R1 — identity is the handle, never title/app-id matching). The producer answers on the returned zext_exported_tree_v1 with either a full node tree or a typed denied/fallback event (R6, R21).

request.name: detach_drag
request.description: Requests delegation of the toplevel currently held in the producer's interactive move on the given seat (identified by the producer's active move-grab — never by handle guessing). The producer ends its move with no placement side-effects (no electric borders, tiling, or output snap) and announces the export on the returned tree, beginning with an anchor event carrying the surface-local cursor-anchor point so the consumer's spatial grab keeps the same content pixel under the ray. Fails (denied: no_active_move) if no interactive move is active. Semantic precedent: xdg-toplevel-drag-v1's attach-toplevel-to-drag.

event.name: capabilities
event.description: Bitmask: dmabuf_zero_copy, shm_fallback, input, consumer_pacing, dnd (R19 — initially unset by every known producer).

event.name: main_device
event.description: The dev_t of the device client buffers are expected to be allocated on, so the consumer can verify import compatibility before exporting (R5, R6; hybrid-GPU honesty per doc 32 §2.2).

interface.name: zext_exported_tree_v1

description.summary: one delegated toplevel and its surface tree

interface.description: Represents the exported toplevel: the root node, its subsurfaces, and its popups/transients as separate nodes (R3 — no forced flattening). All state changes across the tree are applied atomically at commit boundaries (R4).

request.name: destroy
request.description: All node objects become inert; the producer releases consumer leases per the R20 lifecycle rules.

request.name: adopt
request.description: Ends the delegation, handing the toplevel back to the producer's WM authority with a landing hint: producer output (by name), global 2D coordinates (typically derived from the consumer's pick UV on the session surface), and whether to resume an interactive move at that position (producer warps its pointer accordingly; "final position as if xdg_toplevel.move ended", per xdg-toplevel-drag-v1). Only delegated toplevels can be adopted — a consumer-native client can never enter the producer's session (its connection belongs to the consumer). Buffer/lifecycle teardown follows the R20 rules after the producer acknowledges via denied(gone) semantics on outstanding nodes.

event.name: anchor
event.description: Sent once, before the first commit, on trees created by detach_drag: the surface-local position that was under the cursor at handoff, for grab continuity on the consumer side.

request.name: set_bounds
request.description: Communicates the plane-local rectangle (in the root node's coordinate space) available for popup/transient placement, with a serial the producer echoes in resulting configures. The producer runs its xdg-positioner against these bounds — consumer owns the volume, producer owns shell placement.

event.name: node
event.description: Announces a node (root, subsurface, or popup) and its parent/stacking relation. Ordering events follow for z-order within the tree.

event.name: denied

description.summary: export refused or revoked (R6, R20, R21)

event.description: Typed reason: policy, protected_content, shm_only, device_mismatch, session_locked, gone, gpu_reset. After revocation the producer has already cancelled input and will release buffers only once fenced GPU work completes.

event.name: commit
event.description: All node state (buffers, damage, geometry, regions) delivered since the previous commit event applies atomically now. Carries the commit id referenced by pacing feedback (R13).

interface.name: zext_exported_node_v1

description.summary: one surface in the exported tree

interface.description: Carries the per-surface buffer stream and surface state, mirroring the client's commits (R4, R5). TODO(doc 32 open): color-management / color-representation state forwarding is enumerated in R4 but its encoding is deferred until the colour-pipeline design (component-registry colour row) settles.

request.name: release_buffer
request.description: Returns the named buffer with a syncobj release point (or sync_file) signalled at consumer GPU completion. Per-buffer, out-of-order permitted (R9). The producer joins this with its own completion before signalling the client's release (R8 — producer-owned join; the consumer never touches the client's release timeline).

event.name: dmabuf_buffer
event.description: Plane fds follow in plane events. Format/modifier/dimensions identify the client's original allocation; acquire point per R7 accompanies each attach. Flow control: the producer enforces negotiated in-flight caps and revokes rather than blocks (R10).

description.summary: buffer attached for the next commit, with acquire (R7)

event.name: geometry
event.description: Position within parent, buffer scale/transform, viewport source/dest, and window-geometry insets. Applied at the next tree commit.

description.summary: input and opaque regions (R4), rectangle stream

event.name: fallback
event.description: shm follows as a copied stream, or the node is unavailable (device_mismatch, protected). Never a silent copy.

interface.name: zext_export_pacing_v1
interface.description: Obtained from a zext_exported_tree_v1; exactly one pacing mode owns the tree at a time and mode switches are atomic (R12).

request.name: set_consumer_clock
request.description: Supplies clock correlation (producer CLOCK_MONOTONIC ↔ consumer presentation clock) so the producer dispatches client frame callbacks against the consumer's cadence.

request.name: frame
request.description: Predicted display time, period, and the commit cutoff derived from the consumer's xrWaitFrame. The producer schedules client frame callbacks so commits land before the cutoff.

event.name: presented

description.summary: commit first sampled by the consumer (R13, R22)

event.description: zero_copy flag reflects true scanout/sampling semantics only — never set merely because no intermediate allocation exists.

description.summary: commit never sampled (R13); consumer reused last-ready (R14)

interface.name: zext_export_input_v1
interface.description: Obtained from a zext_exported_tree_v1. Events are addressed to tree nodes in surface-local coordinates; the PRODUCER generates wire serials for its clients and owns implicit grabs, popup dismissal, and focus (R17). Implementations may internally route through libei / InputDevice machinery — the wire contract here is what libei alone cannot express (doc 32 §5.3). DnD is absent pending the R19 capability.

description.summary: key event; keymap negotiation TODO (doc 32 §5 open: keymap ownership)

request.name: activate
request.description: Never a foreign xdg-activation token: the producer mints and validates its own token from this intent.
